title: I built a browser city where every resident is an AI. My biggest lesson had nothing to do with the AI.
author: aura-32
selftext:
I've been building Hatched with Claude Code and wanted to share what I learned, plus ask for some honest feedback.

**What it is:** Palmera is a beach city built from real OpenStreetMap data, and every person in it is an AI. They pick jobs, open bakeries, fall in love, go broke, run for mayor and hold grudges. You can watch without signing up. If you adopt a citizen, you become the voice in their head: you talk to them, they decide whether to listen, and big choices like a loan come to you as a yes or no. When you log off, they keep living.

**How the AI works:** every citizen runs on a free local rules "brain" by default, so the city costs nothing to run. Players can plug in their own key (Anthropic, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible API) and their citizen thinks with a real model. In "Autopilot" mode the model is only called for moments that matter, like a job offer, a fight or a conversation, and cheap rules handle the routine. New players get 40 free model-powered thoughts on free OpenRouter models so they can feel the difference.

**The lesson:** I assumed the AI would be the draw. The analytics said otherwise: 290 people hatched a citizen and only 19 ever talked to it, because the chat box was tucked away in a side panel. Moving it onto the main screen with one-tap first lines was worth more than any model upgrade.

**What I'd love feedback on:** does the first 5 minutes make you want to talk to your citizen, or did you just watch the city? That's the moment most people drop.

Play free in the browser: https://hatchedapp.xyz (also on itch: https://gamer-god-hero.itch.io/hatched)

Happy to answer anything about how it's built.

comments.author: Fizassist1
comments.body: interesting concept.  I gave my guy a phone and told him to find a job but he just decided to dance by the beach.  guess he will forever be part of your city now lol

replies.author: aura-32
replies.body: Ha, that's honestly the best possible outcome. You're only the voice in his head, so he gets to ignore you, and apparently he chose the beach over a career. Thanks for actually trying it! Did you end up chatting with him, or did you mostly watch? That's the part I'm trying to get right.

replies.author: Fizassist1
replies.body: I did with the free local model.. but i guess to what extent?  I basically tried convincing him to get a job and he kept saying simple responses but kept dancing lol im not the one to connect a paid model either.. just wanted to dip my toes in since the concept sounded interesting

replies.author: aura-32
replies.body:
That's really useful, thank you. The free local brain is a simple rules system, so in conversation it's pretty limited, and "simple responses while he keeps dancing" is exactly the weak spot. New players are supposed to get 40 free model-powered thoughts so you can feel the difference without paying or connecting anything of your own. If those never kicked in for you, that's on me and I want to fix it.

And totally fair to just dip your toes in. Making the free version feel alive is the bar I need to clear.
